rules.name: Separable equation pattern
preconditions: h(y) is nonzero on the working domain
rules.operation: Separate variables to reduce a first-order ODE to two integrals.
examples: Equations of the form y' = xy reduce to dy/y = x dx on regions where y is nonzero
counterexamples: Separating terms that are not multiplicatively factored is invalid

rules.name: Linear first-order integrating factor rule
preconditions: p and q are defined on the active interval
rules.operation: Multiply by an integrating factor to convert the equation into a product derivative.
examples: Integrating factors convert the left side into the derivative of a product
counterexamples: Using an integrating factor unrelated to p(x) is invalid

rules.name: Constant-coefficient characteristic equation rule
rules.output_form: solution form from roots of ar^2 + br + c = 0
preconditions: a is nonzero
rules.operation: Solve the characteristic polynomial to determine the homogeneous solution type.
examples: Distinct real roots produce a linear combination of exponentials
counterexamples: Ignoring multiplicity of repeated roots is invalid

rules.name: Equilibrium point criterion for autonomous ODEs
rules.output_form: equilibrium solutions at zeros of f
preconditions: The equation is autonomous
rules.operation: Identify equilibrium solutions by locating zeros of the vector field.
examples: Constant solutions arise where the vector field vanishes
counterexamples: Taking a point with f(y_*) not equal to 0 as an equilibrium is invalid

rules.name: Picard-Lindelof existence-uniqueness seed
rules.input_form: initial value problem y' = f(x,y), y(x_0)=y_0
rules.output_form: local existence and uniqueness under standard hypotheses
preconditions: f is continuous and locally Lipschitz in y on the working region
rules.operation: Use standard regularity hypotheses to guarantee a unique local solution.
examples: Well-behaved right-hand sides admit a unique local solution through the initial point
counterexamples: Claiming uniqueness without the needed regularity hypotheses is invalid in general

rules.name: Variation of parameters seed
rules.input_form: nonhomogeneous linear differential equation with homogeneous basis
preconditions: A fundamental homogeneous solution family is known and the standard method hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Allow homogeneous solution coefficients to vary in order to solve forced linear equations.
examples: Variation of parameters extends homogeneous solution data to forced equations
counterexamples: Keeping the coefficients constant in a genuinely forced equation is invalid

rules.name: Matrix exponential rule for linear systems
preconditions: A is a constant matrix
rules.operation: Represent constant-coefficient linear system evolution by a matrix exponential.
examples: Constant-coefficient linear systems evolve through matrix exponentials
counterexamples: Replacing e^(tA) by I + tA alone is invalid except as a first-order approximation

rules.name: Separation-of-variables seed for the heat equation
preconditions: The domain and boundary conditions fit the standard separation method
rules.operation: Reduce a heat equation by product ansatz to eigenfunction and exponential factor equations.
examples: Rectangular and interval domains often reduce the heat equation to eigenfunction expansions by separation of variables
counterexamples: Assuming every boundary-value problem separates without the needed structure is invalid

rules.name: d'Alembert formula seed
rules.input_form: one-dimensional wave equation on the line
preconditions: The problem is posed on the whole line with the standard one-dimensional wave hypotheses
rules.operation: Split a wave solution into left- and right-moving components.
examples: d'Alembert decomposition splits a line-wave solution into left- and right-moving components
counterexamples: Applying the formula unchanged on bounded domains with boundary conditions is invalid

rules.name: Linearization stability seed
rules.input_form: equilibrium of a smooth autonomous system
rules.output_form: stability inference from linearization under standard spectral hypotheses
preconditions: The Jacobian at the equilibrium is defined and the standard linearization theorem hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Use local linear spectral data to infer nearby stability behavior.
examples: Eigenvalues with negative real part indicate local asymptotic stability in the standard linearization theorem setting
counterexamples: Linearization is inconclusive in general when eigenvalues lie on the imaginary axis
